Global situation The mpox global situation update is provided monthly. For the latest information (as of August 2024) please refer to the following report: Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #37 - 22 September 2024 (who.int) 8 The first mpox cases were detected in Burundi in July 2024. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Individual-level risk is largely dependent on individual factors such as exposure risk and immune status, regardless of geographic area, epidemiological context, biological sex, gender identity or sexual orientation. In the last week 402 new confirmed cases and no new deaths were reported. In addition to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, deaths among confirmed mpox cases in 2024 have been reported in South Africa (three), Cameroon (two), Central African Republic (one) and Cote d’Ivoire (one). Among the countries reporting mpox in 2024, all 15 countries have reported new confirmed cases within the past six weeks (see Figure 1, right). The six weeks refer to two mpox incubation periods of 21 days. In the past month, one country, Guinea, reported its first mpox case. Figure 1. Nevertheless, the epidemic curve in Figure 2 may underrepresent the epidemiological situation given the limited testing capacities in several African countries, especially in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where from January to September 2024 around 37% of suspected cases have been tested, with a test positivity of 54%. Available sequencing data has identified clade Ib MPXV in three provinces, South Kivu, North Kivu and Kinshasa. Clade Ib MPXV was first identified in January 2024 in South Kivu, a province unaffected by mpox prior to September 2024; clade Ib MPXV is associated with a rapid rise in case reports in the province. MPXV clade Ib and clade Ia were found to be cocirculating in Kinshasa in July-August 2024.5 In 2024, the provinces reporting the highest number of suspected mpox cases are Equateur and South Kivu, followed by Sankuru, Sud Ubangi, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Mongala (Figure 4, left). The same provinces have also reported the highest number of confirmed mpox cases in 2024 (Figure 4, right). Global situation The mpox global situation update is provided monthly. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Available sequencing data has identified clade Ib MPXV in three provinces, South Kivu, North Kivu and Kinshasa. Clade Ib MPXV was first identified in January 2024 in South Kivu, a province unaffected by mpox prior to September 2024; clade Ib MPXV is associated with a rapid rise in case reports in the province. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Focus on Burundi Since the onset of the outbreak in July 2024, the virus has spread geographically in Burundi where 35 of the 49 (71%) national districts have been affected (Figure 6, left). The three districts of Bujumbura city are the most affected, accounting for around 60% of the national cases. In the last four weeks, 32 districts (65%) have reported at least one confirmed mpox case (Figure 6, right). Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 8 Figure 6. Geographic distribution of confirmed mpox cases, by district, Burundi, from July 8 to 22 September 2024 (left), and from 26 August to 22 September 2024 (right). As of 22 September 2022, 54% of confirmed cases in Burundi are male. The most affected age groups are adults and children under 5 years of age, with the latter comprising around 30% of confirmed cases Since the outbreak began, of the 1879 suspected mpox cases, 1743 (93%) were tested; among these, 696 were confirmed by PCR (positivity 40%) (Figure 7) with test positivity rising in recent weeks. Figure 7. Epidemic curve of suspected and confirmed mpox cases and positivity rate, by week, Burundi, 22 July – 22 September (epidemiological week 30-38) 2024. Global situation The mpox global situation update is provided monthly. For the latest information (as of August 2024) please refer to the following report: Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #37 - 22 September 2024 (who.int) 8 The first mpox cases were detected in Burundi in July 2024. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow. Epidemic curve of reported suspected mpox cases (tested and untested) in Africa, by reporting country, 1 January 2024 – 22 September 2024 Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 6 Focus on the Democratic Republic of the Congo In 2024, all provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reported suspected mpox cases. Available sequencing data has identified clade Ib MPXV in three provinces, South Kivu, North Kivu and Kinshasa. Clade Ib MPXV was first identified in January 2024 in South Kivu, a province unaffected by mpox prior to September 2024; clade Ib MPXV is associated with a rapid rise in case reports in the province. MPXV clade Ib and clade Ia were found to be cocirculating in Kinshasa in July-August 2024.5 In 2024, the provinces reporting the highest number of suspected mpox cases are Equateur and South Kivu, followed by Sankuru, Sud Ubangi, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Mongala (Figure 4, left). The same provinces have also reported the highest number of confirmed mpox cases in 2024 (Figure 4, right). Trends in suspected cases reveal important differences between provinces6 – the number of weekly reported cases in Equateur is stable, with approximately 100 - 200 suspected cases reported per week, while the trend in South Kivu continues to rise with around 500 - 600 cases reported per week. Weekly reported cases are also increasing in Sankuru, Sud Ubangi, Tshopo, Tshuapa and Mongala. While the higher number of reported mpox cases may in part be attributable to strengthened surveillance, there is also evidence to support rising mpox transmission in the country in recent years.7 Figure 4. Geographic distribution of reported suspected (left) and confirmed (right) mpox cases, by province, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 1 January – 15 September 2024. 5 Co-circulation of monkeypox virus subclades Ia and Ib in Kinshasa Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, July to August 2024 https://www.eurosurveillance.org/content/10.2807/1560-7917.ES.2024.29.38.2400592 6Report of the epidemiological situation of mpox in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, sitrep No 026 (from 9 to 15 September 2024) [French] https://reliefweb.int/report/democratic-republic-congo/rapport-de-la-situation-epidemiologique-de-la-variole-simienne-mpox-en-rdc-sitrep-no-026-du-09-au-15-septembre-2024 7 Mpox in the Democratic Republic of Congo: Analysis of National Epidemiological and Laboratory Surveillance Data, 2010 – 2023 https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4954317 Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 7 Most mpox deaths among suspected cases in the country are reported in the provinces of Equateur, Sankuru, Tshuapa and Tshopo (Figure 5). The case fatality ratio (CFR) differs between provinces, with the highest recorded in Maindombe (6.7%) and Equateur (5.3%), while some provinces with low number of mpox cases have not reported any death in 2024 so far (Figure 5). In South Kivu, which is believed to be affected only by clade Ib MPXV, and to date primarily among adults, the CFR is 0.5%. Figure 5. Geographic distribution of mpox deaths among suspected cases, by province, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 1 January – 15 September 2024. Focus on Burundi Since the onset of the outbreak in July 2024, the virus has spread geographically in Burundi where 35 of the 49 (71%) national districts have been affected (Figure 6, left). The three districts of Bujumbura city are the most affected, accounting for around 60% of the national cases. In the last four weeks, 32 districts (65%) have reported at least one confirmed mpox case (Figure 6, right). Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 8 Figure 6. Geographic distribution of confirmed mpox cases, by district, Burundi, from July 8 to 22 September 2024 (left), and from 26 August to 22 September 2024 (right). As of 22 September 2022, 54% of confirmed cases in Burundi are male. The most affected age groups are adults and children under 5 years of age, with the latter comprising around 30% of confirmed cases Since the outbreak began, of the 1879 suspected mpox cases, 1743 (93%) were tested; among these, 696 were confirmed by PCR (positivity 40%) (Figure 7) with test positivity rising in recent weeks. Figure 7. Epidemic curve of suspected and confirmed mpox cases and positivity rate, by week, Burundi, 22 July – 22 September (epidemiological week 30-38) 2024. Global situation The mpox global situation update is provided monthly. For the latest information (as of August 2024) please refer to the following report: Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #37 - 22 September 2024 (who.int) 8 The first mpox cases were detected in Burundi in July 2024. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 9 Global operational updates The WHO health emergency prevention, preparedness, response and resilience (HEPR) framework underpins both the Strategic Framework for enhancing prevention and control of mpox (2024-2027) and the current emergency response to the mpox Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Aligned with the HEPR framework, the WHO Global Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP) for mpox focuses on strengthening five core components—the 5Cs: 1. Emergency coordination: Efficient coordination for timely crisis response. 2. Collaborative surveillance: Real-time data integration for early threat detection. 3. Community protection: Engaging communities in prevention and resilience-building measures. 4. Safe and scalable care: Equipping health systems to provide essential care with scalable capacity. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures: Ensuring equitable distribution of medical countermeasures. This section provides updates on the WHO global mpox response as of 22 September 2024. 1. Emergency coordination • Through its Country Offices WHO is supporting Member States in operationalizing response plan guided by the Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan (SPRP). Coordinating with Partners WHO is supporting national coordination structures including activated Incident Management Systems (IMS) in technical areas such as surveillance and epidemiological analysis, vaccination, infection prevention and control (IPC), risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), treatment and therapeutics, operation support and logistics (OSL), among others. On request of Member States, WHO AFRO Regional Office and headquarters have deployed experts to support response operations. • WHO is still working with relevant partners to design research activities for a better understanding of the outbreak and evidence-based strategies (refer to special focus below). 2. Collaborative surveillance • Epidemiological data on mpox updated weekly can be accessed on the WHO surveillance report here. • WHO updated the template transmission studies protocol to support mpox field investigations. • A webinar on the use of digital and analytics tools for mpox response was held on 24 September 2024. Countries shared their experience using Go.Data for mpox response. Analytical tools and initiatives highlighted included the Collaboratory epidemiological parameters for modelling and analysis, and software tools for addressing common analytics tasks. • An EPI-WIN webinar on collaborative surveillance for mpox was held on 26 September 2024. WHO and Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shared updates on current mpox global surveillance, the main activities to support countries with mpox surveillance, persisting challenges and an update of the current epidemiological situation. • WHO convened the Orthopoxvirus Laboratory Network to review and update interim guidance on diagnostic testing for monkeypox virus (MPXV). The upcoming update to this interim guidance shall include the latest guidance on MPXV near-point-of-care tests and antigen rapid diagnostic tests. • WHO and partners initiated the diagnostics workstream of the Access and Allocation Mechanism (AAM). 3. Community protection • Coordination for community protection continues, covering risk communication, RCCE and infodemic management; community IPC; water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH); home-based care; vaccination; border health and mass gatherings; and managing risks of transmission between animals and humans. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 10 Key multi-partner and civil society engagement and advocacy meetings were held in the reporting period: • The Community Protection Partners Network meeting held on 20 September 2024 focused on home-based care and community-based infection prevention and control, especially for low resource settings. • The informal community reference group of civil society organizations, networks and researchers was held on 20 September with representatives from 15 Countries from WHO AFRO, EURO and PAHO regions. Community representatives emphasized the importance of 1) ensuring that messages reach key populations, especially communities affected by HIV, and 2) community preparedness and involvement in the response to address complex layers of stigma and discrimination which hamper efforts to reach key populations and other marginalized groups. Special efforts are required to reach people with disabilities. • The Collective Service is an interagency initiative between IFRC, UNICEF, WHO, and GOARN for the coordinated delivery of RCCE for public health emergencies. A bi-monthly global call provides a platform for partners to share and hear updates on the global situation. 4. Safe and scalable care • A rapid assessment tool for IPC and WASH in health facilities has been shared with the African Regional Office and affected countries. This is being implemented in many health facilities in hotspot areas to identify opportunities for improvement in IPC practices and WASH services to ensure health workers and patients remain safe while receiving care. • Posters for health and care workers for putting on and removing PPE for mpox are available on the WHO website. Steps to put on PPE for mpox, Steps to remove PPE for mpox. 5. Access to and delivery of countermeasures Vaccines • On 19 September 2024, the European Medicines Agency recommended extending the indication of Modified vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) smallpox/mpox vaccine to include adolescents 12 to 17 years of age. • The WHO Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety met on 20 September to review available safety data on mpox vaccines and WHO protocols for safety monitoring. Diagnostics • In working towards emergency use listing of mpox diagnostics EUL, WHO is conducting a bridged assessment of 2 dossiers and expecting another dossier submission in coming days. • On 25 September 2024, WHO met with representatives from Ghana, Nigeria, Rwanda and Tanzania to explore coordination on vaccine safety surveillance data and sharing of data. Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report n.38 11 Special focus A coordinated research roadmap for monkeypox virus: Immediate research next steps to contribute to control the outbreak From 29-30 August, 2024, the Africa CDC, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the United States National Institutes of Health (US NIH) and WHO held a scientific conference aimed at aligning research efforts with the practical needs of mpox outbreak control. In a comprehensive effort to synchronize research initiatives with the immediate requirements of mpox outbreak management, discussions emphasized collaboration, regulatory and ethics considerations, and national leadership. Over 2500 participants from affected countries and around the world— scientists, Member State representatives, public health professionals, funding agencies and private sector representatives— gathered to accelerate development of innovations to control the mpox epidemic. The meeting aimed to develop an emergency mpox research response agenda, enhance collaboration and partnerships, and outline key steps and timelines for addressing research gaps, emphasizing the leading role of affected countries and their researchers in shaping the research agenda. Key principles guiding the meeting included collaboration, leadership from affected regions, alignment with outbreak response goals, and a people-centered focus. There was consensus on the need for studies that 1) contribute to controlling the outbreak; 2) guide interventions so that those at the highest risk of infection are protected, promptly diagnosed, and receive optimal care; and 3) catalyze integration of research in each area of outbreak response, in a collaborative manner and with researchers and ministries of health of the affected countries in the driving seat. Ten immediate next steps for a coordinated Research Roadmap: 1. Obtain additional data on mpox transmission and epidemiology, including clinical outcomes and risk factors for severe disease. 2. Evaluate and deploy new rapid and sensitive diagnostic tests that detect all monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades and help with the differential diagnosis of diseases that can resemble mpox. 3. Define and implement all elements of an optimized clinical standard of care for all mpox patients. 4. Promote development of new therapeutics and evaluation of safety and efficacy of prioritized candidate therapeutics for mpox, in coordinated collaborative multicenter trials. 5. Conduct research on animal models and use animal models towards the determination of correlates of protection, and support research on immunoassays. 6. Define regulatory pathways for “next generation” medical countermeasures. 7. Facilitate availability of vaccines in areas with sustained human to human transmission as part of an integrated response, and promote generation of critical data regarding vaccine safety, performance and delivery strategies. 8. Use existing tools to incorporate Good Participatory Practices and community engagement in research including public health research. 9. Integrate research into outbreak response activities. 10. Embrace and expand opportunities for coordination and collaboration of all research initiatives with local authorities and research institutions, with researchers from affected countries and ministries of health at the centre of the response. A summary of these immediate next steps can be found here. A full research roadmap will follow.
