    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."

News Activities ### We speak out. Get updates. # Mpox outbreak in DR Congo: What to know A recent surge of mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) infections in DR Congo is cause for alarm. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."

The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record.     "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record.     "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023.     "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

}

Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) ![CDC Logo](/TemplatePackage/4.0/assets/imgs/logo/logo-notext.svg) # Monkeypox Caused by Human-to-Human Transmission of *Monkeypox Virus* in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with Spread to Neighboring Countries ![Health Alert Network logo.](/han/images/HAN-Logo240x116px.png?_=71758) ![HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125](/han/images/HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png?_=71757 \"HAN_badge_HEALTH_UPDATE_320x125.png\") Distributed via the CDC Health Alert Network August 7, 2024, 3:15 PM ET CDCHAN-00513 **Summary** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is issuing this Health Alert Network (HAN) Health Update to provide additional information about the outbreak of monkeypox virus (MPXV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC); the first [Health Advisory](https://emergency.cdc.gov/han/2023/han00501.asp) about this outbreak was released in December 2023. Since January 2023, the DRC has reported the largest number of yearly suspected clade I monkeypox cases on record. While clade I MPXV is endemic, or naturally occurring, in DRC, the current outbreak is more widespread than any previous DRC outbreak and has resulted in clade I monkeypox transmission to some neighboring countries."

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."
  ]
}

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases."

    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

    "## Content Search Informing humanitarians worldwide 24/7 — a service provided by UN OCHA [DR Congo](/country/cod) + 14 more # Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #42 - 9 November 2024 Format : Situation Report Source : * [WHO](/organization/who) Posted Originally published Origin : [View original](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/multi-country-outbreak-of-mpox--external-situation-report--42--9-november-2024) ## Attachments * [![Preview of 20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf](/sites/default/files/styles/small/public/previews/f6/23/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059.png?2584935-1-0) **Download Report** (PDF | 1.2 MB)](/attachments/f6238fd2-5642-432e-a66f-09905adce059/20241109_mpox_external-sitrep_-42.pdf) **Highlights** • Since the last situation report, three additional countries have confirmed travel-related cases of clade Ib MPXV: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, Zambia and Zimbabwe. • For the first time, local transmission of clade Ib MPXV was reported outside of Africa, in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, where three (all) household members of the initial case (who had travelled to affected East African countries with clade Ib) were confirmed to have mpox. • The number of mpox cases in Africa shows a general rising trend, driven mainly by cases reported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and Uganda. • As of 3 November 2024, Clade Ib monkeypox virus (MPXV) has been detected in six provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: South Kivu, North Kivu, Kinshasa, Kasai, Tshopo and Tanganyika, with no new areas known to be affected since the last update. Additionally, 11 other countries have also reported clade Ib MPXV cases.",
    "Mpox: Multi-country External Situation Report no.57 1 Mpox Multi-country external situation report no. 57 published 28 August 2025 KEY FIGURES Area Number of reported confirmed cases Number of deaths among confirmed cases Number of reporting countries Global (1 Jan – 31 July 2025)* 34 386 138 84 Key countries (1 Jan – 17 August 2025) Democratic Republic of the Congo 15 377 30 - Uganda 6522 35 - Sierra Leone 5149 52 - Burundi 1394 0 - * Most recent global surveillance data available. Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries. When mpox outbreaks are not rapidly contained and human-to-human transmission is not interrupted, they continue to pose a risk of sustained community transmission. Since the last edition of this report, one country, Senegal, has reported mpox for the first time. Efforts to identify the clade are underway. • Furthermore, Türkiye has reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib MPXV for the first time and the Democratic Republic of Congo has reported its first cases of mpox due to clade IIb MPXV. • In July 2025, 47 countries in five (out of six) WHO regions reported a total of 3924 confirmed cases, including 30 deaths (case fatality ratio [CFR] 0.8%). The South-East Asian and Western Pacific regions reported an increase in cases in July 2025, while the African Region, European Region and the Region of the Americas reported a decrease. The Eastern Mediterranean Region did not report any mpox case in July 2025. • Twenty-one countries in Africa have reported ongoing mpox transmission in the past six weeks. Clade IIb MPXV continues to be reported in West Africa, while Central African countries report both clade Ia and clade Ib MPXV, and East African countries report clade Ib MPXV."
  ]
}

Here’s what to know and why we need a comprehensive response. ### Share ![Mpox Cases Amidst Displacement Sites Near Goma](/sites/default/files/styles/crop_article_mobile_335_189/public/image_base_media/2024/09/MSB205871.jpg?h=b31044db&itok=ACy3roai) MSF health promoter Aristote Saidi Wanyama uses a poster and megaphone to share information about mpox prevention strategies in Buhimba displacement camp on the outskirts of Goma, North Kivu. **|** DR Congo 2024 © Michel Lunanga Related Related The [mpox](/what-we-do/medical-issues/mpox \"Mpox\") epidemic currently sweeping through [Democratic Republic of Congo](/what-we-do/where-we-work/democratic-republic-congo \"Democratic Republic of Congo\") (DRC) is spreading at an alarming rate—and has been reported beyond DRC's borders. Since the beginning of this year, there have been close to 20,000 cases of mpox and over 630 deaths, according to Congolese authorities. While epidemic outbreaks are generally concentrated in the center and northwest of the country, confirmed cases of mpox have now been reported in the [eastern provinces](/latest/conflict-dr-congo-whats-happening-how-help \"Conflict in DR Congo: What’s happening & how to help\") of South and North Kivu, where almost a million displaced people are l"
  ]
}

Highlights • All clades of monkeypox virus (MPXV) continue to circulate in several countries.
